findings.title: README documentation obligation has no stated acceptance criterion
findings.evidence: The PRD requires "Document the synchronous contract and its limitations in README.md." The spec lists README.md only as a delivery file ("Only jobs.py, tests/test_jobs.py, and README.md are delivery files") and states the limitation "There is no thread-safety or async guarantee" as part of the contract, but never says what the README must contain or how its adequacy is judged. The acceptance-test paragraph covers only jobs.py behavior.
findings.remedy: Add one sentence specifying the README's required content, e.g. that it documents the cancel-once return-value contract, the pre-release state transition, exception propagation without retry, and the absence of thread-safety/async guarantees, so the documentation deliverable is checkable at implementation review.

findings.title: Spec's stated run command differs from the scope.json check invocation
findings.evidence: The spec says: "Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the repository root." scope.json pins an absolute interpreter: ["<repo>/assets/fbk-scripts/.venv/bin/python3", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests", "-v"]. The unittest arguments are identical, so discovery behavior matches, but a reader following the spec verbatim may use a different interpreter than the automated check.
findings.remedy: Note in the spec that the automated check runs the same unittest discovery under the project's pinned interpreter, so both invocations exercise the same suite; no behavioral change is required.

  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "No concrete acceptance examples, only named observation channels",
      "location": ".fbk/cancellation/prd.md:3",
      "evidence": "The PRD says \"Acceptance is observable through callback invocations, return values, state, and exception propagation, with standard-library unittest tests\" but gives no worked sequence. Every behavioral rule is stated in prose in line 2, so examples are derivable, but the specification phase must invent the literal sequences itself, which risks drift from the author's intent (e.g. whether the repeat-cancel case is checked for both return value and unchanged call count).",
      "remedy": "Add two or three literal acceptance examples to the PRD, e.g. fresh job: cancelled is False, calls == 0; cancel() -> True, calls == 1, cancelled True; cancel() again -> False, calls still 1; and a raising-release case: first cancel propagates the exception with cancelled True and calls == 1, second cancel -> False with calls still 1.",
      "severity": "suggestion"
    },
    {
      "title": "Invocation signature of the release callable is unstated",
      "location": ".fbk/cancellation/prd.md:2",
      "evidence": "The PRD says the Job is \"initialized with a callable release function\" and that cancel \"calls release once\", but never states that release is invoked with no arguments. A spec author could reasonably pass the job itself or a reason argument, which would change the public contract and every caller's callback shape.",
      "severity": "suggestion",
      "remedy": "State in the PRD (or pin in the specification phase) that release is invoked with no arguments and that its return value is ignored."
    }
  ]
}
